image.alt: A Philodendron Brasil in a white textured pot, its heart-shaped leaves split down the middle by a bold lime stripe

light.label: Bright indirect light
light.note: Tolerates medium light, but new leaves come back plainer

landscape_use.note: Frost-free zones, out of direct sun

snap: A fast, trailing Philodendron with heart-shaped leaves split down the middle by a bold lime stripe — the green and gold of the flag it is named for. Forgiving enough for a first plant, it trails from a shelf or climbs a pole, and is toxic to cats and dogs if chewed.

deep_dive.title: Origin & Habit
deep_dive.body: A variegated form of the common heartleaf Philodendron from Central America and the Caribbean — the same species as the velvet-leaved Micans, wearing a quite different coat. It grows quickly either way: trailing from a shelf, or climbing a pole with bigger leaves each time.

deep_dive.title: Key Care Rule
deep_dive.body: Water when the top inch of soil has dried. This is among the most forgiving houseplants sold — it wilts plainly when thirsty and recovers within hours of a drink — which is what makes it a sensible first plant.

deep_dive.title: Special Feature
deep_dive.body: No two leaves carry the same amount of lime: some come out almost entirely green, others nearly all stripe. Bright indirect light keeps the contrast sharp, and a stem that runs all-green can be cut back to a variegated node to bring the colour home.

deep_dive.title: Pet Safety
deep_dive.body: Toxic to cats and dogs if chewed or swallowed; the calcium oxalate crystals irritate the mouth and stomach. Trailing stems hang within easy reach of a curious cat, so hang it high or keep it to a closed room.
